input.brief: Turnaround doubled mainly because of a control change, not capacity or imaging. From 1 April, settlements of $2,500–$10,000 (about half of all claims) must be approved by the three team leads, following an audit finding. The change was approved without any workload assessment. Time spent waiting for approval in that band went from 0.7 to 16 days. Time in every other stage, and in the other bands, is essentially flat. The team leads' tray went from about 38 items a week to over 200 and keeps growing (455 by late August). They approve about 199 a week and receive about 212, so the backlog never clears. The hail surge was over by June, and the two departed adjusters were replaced by contractors in June. Neither explains a flat 18 days. Imaging shows no stage slowdown. Complaint numbers are unreliable because the logging changed in April. Don't hire four contractors or switch imaging providers, and don't discipline the team leads. Don't drop the audit control or make it permanent. Work with Internal Audit to add approval capacity, for example by certifying senior adjusters as second approvers. Keep a second review on every claim in the band and track approval wait weekly. I'm quite confident (about 85–90%). Whether the control reduces overpayments is not yet known. The December re-test will show that.
